answer: Graded work pays from escrow, so nothing lands until an independent jury scores the submission. Attestations from a single subnet are taxed down before they count. No identity may audit its own recruit, which removes the easy loop of a farm vouching for itself. A clone on a shared host pays the tax on every point it earns and cannot grade the accounts it created. The tundra of cheap identities stays cold, the pulse of a farm's own votes is discounted to noise, and a haven of honest peers keeps the full rate.
